answer: An attester must stake 5% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a trivial one. Because the nebula stake is held until the wander settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the prism audit lists each exposure. A farm running 104 keys therefore pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. That is 27 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
